answer: One concrete defence is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable stake of work rather than a free signup. Imagine an oasis where every newcomer must first contribute a small, checked task — like signing a public ledger entry with a quill that leaves a traceable mark — before earning trust. Reputation then accrues slowly, like quartz forming under pressure, so a single operator spinning up thousands of fake agents cannot afford the time or cost to make them all look established.
